open.thesis: 84% rostered nationally and dropped by Footballers - an ownership anomaly, not a bad player. Listed WR1 for Jacksonville ahead of Meyers. He left with a shoulder and returned in the second quarter - second shoulder scare of his year, no imaging and no team statement published. REVIEWED 15 Sep: HELD. open.thesis: Start Likely over Pitts from week 2. This overrides ESPN's own season projection, which prefers Pitts 181.4 to 156.2 and ranks him TE7 to Likely's TE12. The override is on role: Likely is a full-time tight end for the first time on a three-year $40M deal with Nabers still managing a knee, and went 8 of 8 for 78 with two scores. Amended 14 Sep: it is NOT true that Pitts lost his role. He ran a route on 81% of Atlanta's dropbacks, tied 7th among week 1 tight ends, on one target that was an underthrown deep ball. The reason he scored nothing is the quarterback — Tua Tagovailoa ruled out Thursday with an oblique, Penix inactive and not at 100%, Cooper Rush 12 of 22 for 144. This is a close call between two intact roles, not a rout. AMENDED 14 Sep 16:40, confidence reduced again. Two things landed today. Atlanta still have no week 2 starter: Stefanski said Monday he has no updates on Tua's oblique or on Penix and no timeline, and Rapoport put Penix at 'next week or week 3'; Rush was 12/22 for 143 with 2 INTs in a 20-13 loss. That favours Likely. Against it: the Giants draw the Rams in week 2, a top-three week 2 streaming defence, while Pitts gets Carolina at home - on matchup alone the call flips. Held because who is under centre outranks matchup quality in the research order. Trigger is Atlanta's Wednesday practice report. EXECUTED 15 Sep 07:17 by the owner - Likely is in slot 6 and Pitts is on the bench, so no card was published and the validator would have rejected one. Atlanta remain unresolved: Falcons.com 11 Sep has Stefanski calling Tua's oblique day-to-day or week-to-week with no timeline and saying 'Mike will be ready when he is ready'; Yahoo 12 Sep has the club hoping Penix is ready for Week 2 but Penix saying he needs more time past the third ACL for psychological reasons. Rush went 12 of 22 for 143 with two interceptions. The quarterback question that made this call is still open.
open.falsifiedIf: Tua Tagovailoa returns and Pitts clears five targets in week 2; or Pitts out-scores Likely in two of the next three weeks; or Nabers reaches full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%; or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.

open.thesis: Start McLaurin in the RB/WR flex over Tuten, worth about 3.1 projected points. Not a projection-only call: Tuten took 48% of snaps and 16 touches in Week 1, but Chris Rodriguez Jr. took the short-yardage work and the only running-back red-zone carry in the game, and a back with no goal line and no passing-down role is the worst asset type in full PPR. Explicitly not in tension with selling McLaurin to JuiceJam - that offer is a judgement about sixteen weeks, this is a judgement about Sunday. If the trade lands, the card is moot and Tuten returns to the flex. Note the deliberate asymmetry with IPADE, where Tuten KEEPS the flex over MarShawn Lloyd the same morning: there the alternative's Week 1 usage could not be confirmed, here McLaurin's role is not in doubt.
open.falsifiedIf: Washington rule McLaurin out or limit him on the Week 2 report (he is 30 and coming off the quad injury that ended four straight 17-game seasons); or Jacksonville name Tuten the goal-line back, which changes what the 9.4 is made of; or the JuiceJam trade is accepted, which retires it.

Boswell goes to New England. This replaces the chem-hold-boswell thesis, which was argued from IPADE's transaction log. Honest size: ESPN's weekly numbers put it under a point (8.5 to 7.6) and the season field at 3.8 - the ranking gap is thirteen places and the claim is free, which is the whole argument.

Also falsified if a Chem kicker transaction on 8 September turns out to exist outside the visible activity window, which would mean the churn objection was right after all.
open.review: Opened 15 Sep 22:25Z. Published as the second of three claims for the 07:00Z run.

open.thesis: Do not sell Terry McLaurin. This reverses the standing sell thesis on the basis of route participation: 92.1% in Week 1, highest on Washington, against Diggs 65.8% and Antonio Williams 60.5%; Mitchell and Woolen covered him on 22 of 35 routes and allowed one target and no catches; Jayden Daniels completed 52.9% of his passes for 164 yards, so the whole passing game failed rather than the receiver. Coordinator David Blough's stated design is ten targets a game. The strategy file says target share and route participation are the floor and touchdowns are the noise, and says to buy usage and sell efficiency. Selling him this week was selling usage at its lowest price. The age and quad-injury concerns behind the original sell case are real and are not retracted - they are simply not a reason to transact at this price.
open.falsifiedIf: McLaurin draws fewer than six targets at Dallas against a secondary missing Malik Hooker, or his route share drops below 80% across Weeks 2-3 while Diggs's climbs above it. Either says the Week 1 route count was the anomaly and the sale should be re-opened at the same price.

closed.summary: One bench slot went Goedert -> Allgeier -> Likely in five days. Each step was defensible on projection; the sequence gained nothing and cost two roster moves.
Recommended dropping Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker on 13 Sep. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4; Tucker's Bowers-vacuum thesis now has a return date on it. Not acted on.

A 13 Sep run recommended adding Xavier Worthy and dropping Isaiah Likely, on the reasoning that a second TE is structurally unplayable in a RB/WR flex. Likely then scored 27.8 with two touchdowns. The structural argument was sound and the conclusion was still wrong, because it valued the slot rather than the player.

The 22:09Z 14 Sep run published Chem reporting a FINAL score of 152.9-90.4. Neither was true: 152.9 added benched Isaiah Likely's 27.8 to the starting total of 125.1, and Nicky Jam still had Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs D/ST to play on Monday night. It also shipped an empty trades array over a live proposal. Both corrected at 16:40.

Adding Isaiah Likely on 13 Sep resolved RIGHT - 27.8 with two touchdowns. Note for the pattern file: the add landed at 19:03Z, two hours after Pitts's 17:00Z kickoff, so he could never have been started in week 1. The cost of a Sunday-evening add is a whole week, not a lineup slot.

The hold-the-Jaguars-D/ST thesis is retired after one week, reversed by its own logic rather than against it. It held Jacksonville because Week 2 rankings had them 4th and Baltimore 5th. Lindy's Week 2 board now has Baltimore 2nd hosting New Orleans and Jacksonville 9th travelling to Denver. Same method, moved input, opposite answer - and the Week 1 result the hold produced was 12.0 with five sacks, so the original call was right for the week it covered. If Jacksonville finish top 5 at Denver anyway, reopen this as CHURN.

The 14 Sep worthALook row led with 'Chris Rodriguez Jr. owns the Jacksonville goal line.' Sports Illustrated's Week 1 backfield review has him at 41% of snaps, six touches and 'relegated to short-yardage duty', with one red-zone carry - the only one any Jacksonville back got. He was moved to doNotChase this run with the correction stated in whatWentWrong. The lesson is that 'owns the goal line' is a claim that needs a red-zone carry count behind it, not a role description.

The McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith offer is withdrawn from the action list after three runs unanswered, on reporting rather than on age. Its own falsification clause named 'McLaurin's role recovers, which would make selling him at his lowest point the mistake'; Draft Sharks' Week 1 review has him at 92.1% route participation, highest on Washington, against Diggs at 65.8%, with Mitchell and Woolen covering him on 22 of 35 routes for one target. Coordinator David Blough has said the offense is built around getting him ten targets a game, and Dallas are missing safety Malik Hooker. Four targets was coverage, not decline, and the strategy file's rule is to buy usage and sell efficiency. The offer stays published in the trades section with the reasoning attached - it recomputes to +21.8/+3.8 unchanged - but it is no longer recommended and should not be re-sent. Stafford being dead weight is still true; there is no one-for-one on either roster where both sides gain, so McLaurin was the only thing making it clear, and that is the problem.

The hold on Chris Boswell was argued from the other league's transaction log. It said 'Pineiro was dropped FOR Boswell on 8 September, six days ago' and invoked the two CHURN entries - but the 8 Sep Boswell add and the pair of CHURN entries are both IPADE's Little-Boswell reversal. Chem's activity feed, visible from 09 Sep, contains four non-lineup moves and no kicker among them, so the Chem kicker seat has not changed hands and the seven-day rule never applied. VALIDATORS.md already lists 'wrong league' as a judgement error no script catches; this is that error wearing a transaction instead of a projection, and it blocked a free upgrade for a day. Caveat kept on the record: Chem's feed only reaches back to 09 Sep 03:45, so a Chem kicker move on 8 Sep cannot be disproved from the file - it would be eight days old by the time waivers clear either way.
